A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GUIDE and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F. Retained material can be matched reliably across terminology changes, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original OSWorld agent evaluations, component ablations, human evaluations of the retrieval and annotation pipelines, and execution case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds WindowsAgentArena evaluation and new OSWorld and retrieval controls in Tables 2–6.

M1.justification: The retrieval, keyframe extraction, OmniParser processing, frame-pair annotation, knowledge decomposition, and agent integration procedures remain unchanged. Section 3 renames inverse dynamics annotation as VLM pairwise video annotation without changing its inputs, outputs, or operational steps.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates task execution only on OSWorld. v3 adds 154 WindowsAgentArena tasks across six domains, introducing native Windows widgets and a different action interface (Table 2). The original OSWorld coverage remains.

E2.justification: v3 removes the published Watch & Learn-on-Jedi comparison from Table 1 and introduces a distinct Watch & Learn-style raw-trajectory control using Qwen3-VL-8B and GUIDE's retrieved videos (Table 3). It also adds grounding-only and title-only/random retrieval comparators (Tables 3 and 6).

E3.justification: New protocols include a balanced 120-task component study with 12 tasks per domain and a GPT-5.2 annotator, a separate 50-task Qwen3-VL-8B study varying retrieved demonstrations from one to three, and Windows evaluation including Qwen3-VL-32B. The raw-trajectory control specifies two demonstrations, 12 steps each, and a 24K-character cap. Existing OSWorld settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of raw versus decomposed knowledge, grounding alone, subtitle-only annotation, removal of OmniParser, demonstration count, and retrieval ranking alternatives (Tables 3–6). The original grounding-element and annotator-model ablations remain in Appendix C, Table 7, corresponding to v1 Table 3; the failure cases are also retained.

E5.justification: v3 Table 4 newly reports averaging over three random seeds. v1 contains no corresponding seed-averaging statement. This does not establish increased runs for retained experiments; neither version reports dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: The retained GUIDE OSWorld scores are unchanged. New WAA baseline/GUIDE scores are 49.00/59.21 for Agents3+GPT-5.2 and 31.70/44.16 for Qwen3-VL-32B (Table 2). New OSWorld controls score 31.96 for raw trajectories and 34.31 for grounding alone (Table 3). Component, demonstration-count, and retrieval-control results are also added; the original published Jedi comparison is removed.

T1.justification: Equation 1 retains the same annotation function arguments and output, with fIDM renamed fVPA. The revised pairwise-annotation explanation introduces no substantive mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central training-free, plug-and-play contribution remains. v3 corrects the abstract's 'over 5%' improvement claim to +4.47–+7.48 percentage points and replaces the introduction's cross-backbone Watch & Learn superiority claim with a same-backbone style control and an explicit WAA transfer contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 substantially expands attribution: v3 credits structured decomposition over raw trajectories, separates visual annotation from transcript-only guidance, and qualifies OmniParser's contribution as modest under GPT-5.2. It also explains demonstration-count saturation and interprets Windows transfer. The original retrieval-mismatch limitations and failure mechanisms remain in Appendix F.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page pointer announcing code, dataset, and additional results, plus technical details for the new controls, including trajectory limits and the component-study annotator. Existing integration prompts, default pipeline settings, and detailed API cost accounting remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds WindowsAgentArena, Mobile-Env, and three agent-training/tool-use references, and removes the Jedi reference. Its empirical positioning against Watch & Learn becomes a clearly identified style control. The related-work organization and principal distinctions concerning live retrieval, subtitles, and annotation remain.

P1.justification: v3 systematically revises annotation terminology, condenses parts of the method, quality evaluation, and conclusion, and reworks Section 4.3 around additional controls. It adds acknowledgments and a Supplementary Material heading, while preserving the overall section sequence and most existing prose.

P2.justification: New Tables 2–6 substantially expand the experimental presentation. v3 removes the external comparison rows and the original main-text ablation summary while retaining detailed ablations in Appendix C. The eight figures retain their substantive content with label, caption, size, and placement changes; Figure 5's reduced layout crowds its bottom labels against the caption.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important validation gaps in v1 through Windows transfer and same-backbone, component, and retrieval controls (Tables 2–6). These strengthen evidence for generality and identify which parts of GUIDE contribute, while replacing the earlier cross-backbone superiority assertion and retaining the detailed appendices. Limited uncertainty reporting, terse documentation of some new settings, and small presentation regressions remain, but the validation gains are substantial.
